key_insight: AutoGaze autoregressively 'gazes' to select only the most informative spatiotemporal patches before they reach a ViT or MLLM, removing redundancy and dramatically cutting computation for long, high‑resolution videos.
problem_solved: Current MLLMs and ViTs treat every pixel/frame region equally, causing excessive compute and memory use on long, high‑resolution videos with large spatiotemporal redundancy; AutoGaze addresses this inefficiency by pre‑filtering irrelevant patches.
method: Lightweight AutoGaze module placed upstream of a ViT/MLLM that autoregressively selects a minimal set of multi‑scale spatiotemporal patches (gazes) per step.
Training combines next‑token prediction with reinforcement learning to balance task accuracy and the cost of selecting patches, learning where to look over time.
Selected patches are forwarded to the backbone model (ViT/MLLM) while redundant patches are skipped, enabling plug‑and‑play integration with existing video models.
impact: Makes large multimodal video models far more compute‑ and memory‑efficient, enabling scalable long‑form and high‑resolution video understanding in research and production settings while reducing inference cost.

paper_title: Attend Before Attention: Efficient and Scalable Video Understanding via Autoregressive Gazing
paper_authors: Baifeng Shi, Stephanie Fu, Long Lian, Hanrong Ye, David Eigen
